summary: Audit what HoldSpeak functionally does on main today, across six pillars

result.verdict: Four of the five #450 defects are genuinely fixed on current main, each with a named regression test, and the executable one-path census (tests/unit/test_one_path_census.py) now has an EMPTY blocking-findings ledger and passes. Defect 4 (two placement owners) is only half fixed: the backend has one authority with explicit precedence, but the web UI still exposes two independent dials with no override signal, and one describer still reads intel_provider directly instead of the placement authority. That surviving second owner produces a NEW, empirically verified instance of the exact pillar defect: Ask and Recipe-chat runs on this_machine execute the local GGUF while the receipt, the Ask footer bar, and the hub's advertised model manifest all print the CLOUD model id. HoldSpeak still checks one model, runs another, and reports a third.
works: Defect 1 FIXED: this_machine readiness now checks the meeting-intel model the run actually loads, not the dictation backend. holdspeak/inference_targets.py:224-237 calls configured_local_meeting_model_path() (holdspeak/intel/providers.py:277-290), the same path execution pins at holdspeak/inference_targets.py:697-700 -> 641-646. Locked by tests/unit/test_deployment_identity.py:59.

Defect 2 FIXED: the onDevice branch loads THIS profile's model_file (holdspeak/intel/providers.py:816-823), the same artifact readiness attested at holdspeak/inference_targets.py:364-372. Locked by tests/unit/test_deployment_identity.py:84, the explicit 'reports A, runs B, attests A' regression.

Defect 3 FIXED: Ask refuses instead of silently retargeting. holdspeak/services/ask_service.py:107-109 raises model_not_advertised naming the destination and its id; list_models emits one row PER DESTINATION with id (not model name) as the selector, holdspeak/services/ask_service.py:58-79. Locked by tests/unit/test_ask_no_retarget.py (6 tests, all pass).

Defect 5 FIXED: Ask (holdspeak/services/ask_service.py:121-132), Workbench (holdspeak/services/workbench_runner.py:31-33,189,221; holdspeak/services/workbench_service.py:355-376) and Recipe (holdspeak/services/recipe_service.py:70,105,119) all capture an immutable deployment revision and invoke through the SAME kernel InferenceRunner. No bypass path survives.

Defect 4 backend half FIXED: resolve_meeting_placement (holdspeak/intel/providers.py:653-713) is one authority with stated precedence (adopted destination wins over provider intent), consumed by construction (:233), readiness describers (:324), egress boundary (:845) and llm capability (:191). Locked by tests/unit/test_meeting_placement_policy.py (15 tests, pass).

The one-path census fence (tests/unit/test_one_path_census.py:521-570) has NAMED_FINDINGS = {} and FINDINGS_WITHOUT_A_SITE = {}; the fence plus placement-policy plus effect-fence suites run green (59 passed, isolated HOME).
The frozen meeting intel plan does record placement provenance: holdspeak/meeting_session/intel_plan.py:196-198 stamps placement_source, placement_reason and provider_intent into plan metadata.

target_from_profile and this_machine_target both build a single DeploymentIdentity (holdspeak/inference_targets.py:95-117, 443-470) that readiness, execution and placement_receipt (holdspeak/inference_targets.py:182-221) all read from.

broken.title: Ask receipt names the CLOUD model while the run executes the local GGUF (this_machine)
broken.evidence: holdspeak/kernel/prompt_adapter.py:20 reports model as getattr(engine,'active_model','') or getattr(engine,'model',''); MeetingIntel defines NEITHER (holdspeak/intel/engine.py:115-136 assigns model_path/cloud_model and exposes only active_provider), so the adapter always returns ''. holdspeak/services/ask_service.py:105 then sets advertised = self._hub_model() for a this_machine target (prof is None), holdspeak/services/ask_service.py:123 puts it in payload['selected_model'], and holdspeak/services/ask_service.py:149 falls back to it for the receipt. holdspeak/services/sync_service.py:539-542 returns the CLOUD model id whenever meeting.intel_provider == 'cloud'. Execution meanwhile is pinned local: holdspeak/inference_targets.py:697-700 -> 641-646 builds MeetingIntel(provider='local', model_path=revision.model_path). Reproduced live with isolated HOME: intel_provider='cloud', intel_realtime_model=/tmp/local-A.gguf -> this_machine ready=True, deployment.model_path='/tmp/local-A.gguf', executed engine provider/model_path = local /tmp/local-A.gguf, but advertised/receipt model = 'gpt-5-mini'; placement_receipt printed {'target_id':'this_machine','engine':'local','model':'gpt-5-mini'}.
broken.impact: The Ask receipt bar prints the wrong model name to the user: web/src/desk/components/AskPanel.tsx:253-278 renders placement.model in the footer ('RAN ON ... MODEL'). Readiness checked local-A, the run loaded local-A, the receipt says gpt-5-mini. This is the exact #450 class, unfixed.

broken.title: Same wrong-model receipt in Recipe chat
broken.evidence: holdspeak/web/routes/primitives/recipes.py:122 passes default_model=_hub_model_name(ctx) into RecipeService.chat; holdspeak/services/recipe_service.py:102 sets payload['selected_model']=default_model or target.model and holdspeak/services/recipe_service.py:129 stamps actual_placement model=d.get('model') or payload['selected_model'] -- and d['model'] is always '' per prompt_adapter.py:20 above. RecipeService.run is NOT affected (recipe_service.py:126 falls back to target.model, which is the deployment's own name).
broken.impact: Agent chat receipts on the hub-default destination name a model the turn never loaded, and the wrongness is inconsistent between the run and chat verbs of the same agent.

broken.title: Ask's new no-retarget refusal compares against the wrong advertised model
broken.evidence: holdspeak/services/ask_service.py:105-109: advertised comes from _hub_model_name() for this_machine, then an explicit model override is refused when override != advertised with the message "it runs {offer!r}". With intel_provider='cloud' the offer is the cloud model id while the destination actually loads the local GGUF (verified above).
broken.impact: A user who names the model that this_machine genuinely runs (e.g. 'local-A') is refused with 'model not available on This device; it runs gpt-5-mini'. The HS-130-06 honesty fix inherits the upstream lie and turns it into a hard 400.

broken.title: The hub advertises a model name to paired devices that its this_machine deployment does not load
broken.evidence: holdspeak/services/sync_service.py:721-731 appends a live virtual manifest row named from self._hub_model_name(), which reads meeting.intel_provider directly (holdspeak/services/sync_service.py:523-548) and never consults resolve_meeting_placement. With intel_provider='cloud' it advertises the cloud model id; with intel_provider='local' plus an adopted openAICompatible intel_profile_id (which WINS for meetings per holdspeak/intel/providers.py:681-692) it advertises the local GGUF stem while meetings run on the endpoint.
broken.impact: A paired companion asking 'what would run it on your desktop' is told a name that is not what the desktop loads, in both directions of the mismatch.

broken.title: Defect 4 survives in the UI: two placement dials, no precedence and no override signal
broken.evidence: web/src/pages/cores/SettingsCore.tsx:636 renders a Provider cycle over ['meeting','intel_provider'] (options local/cloud, web/src/pages/cores/settingsPrefs.tsx:72); web/src/pages/cores/settingsModels.tsx:414 renders a separate 'Runs on > Meetings' pointer over ['meeting','intel_profile_id'], selectable from every destination (settingsModels.tsx:269-289). The backend precedence (adopted destination beats provider intent) is real -- holdspeak/intel/providers.py:681-692, asserted by tests/unit/test_meeting_placement_policy.py:108 -- and it computes both a source and a reason (holdspeak/intel/providers.py:606-608, 697). Grep of web/src finds NO consumer of placement_source, placement_reason or provider-selection-ignored, and grep of holdspeak/ shows PLACEMENT_PROVIDER_OVERRIDDEN referenced only at providers.py:608,697 plus one test.
broken.impact: A user sets Provider = LOCAL in Settings > Meetings and it silently does nothing because a destination pointer set in a DIFFERENT module wins. The UI shows LOCAL with no override lamp and no reason, so the control lies about what decides placement.

candidates.title: The receipt names what loaded, not what a service guessed
candidates.why: Root-causes four of the five findings above. Give MeetingIntel a real active_model property (set at load time from model_path stem / cloud_model) so prompt_adapter.py:20 stops returning '', and make Ask/Recipe-chat derive selected_model from target.deployment.model instead of _hub_model_name(). candidates.title: Delete _hub_model_name as a placement describer
candidates.why: sync_service.py:523-548 is the last second owner of the placement question outside resolve_meeting_placement. Route it through configured_meeting_deployment() so the hub's advertised manifest, Ask's advertised model, and the actual deployment can never disagree.

candidates.title: One meetings placement dial in the UI
candidates.why: Retire the Provider cycle as a user-facing control (or move it under the Runs on pointer and disable it when a destination is adopted), and surface placement_source/placement_reason from the API so 'PROVIDER SELECTION IGNORED' is visible where the user set it. Ends the silent no-op the owner already paid to fix in the backend.

candidates.title: Executable receipt-honesty fence across every destination kind
candidates.why: Existing tests stub _hub_model_name to 'HubModel-9B' (tests/unit/test_web_routes_ask.py:80 and 7 more, test_web_routes_recipe_chat.py:91), which is why this class regressed unnoticed. A parametrized test that runs the REAL body and asserts readiness-model == executed-model == receipt-model for this_machine / onDevice / openAICompatible / meshNode / hub-default-cloud would make the next instance fail the build.

candidates.title: Close the onDevice blank-model_file fallback
candidates.why: holdspeak/intel/providers.py:820 still falls back to the global meeting model when a profile names no model_file. Today unreachable through a ready target (inference_targets.py:367-369 marks it unavailable), but it is the same shape as the defect just fixed; refuse by name instead, as HS-131-13 did for the local branch.

unknown: Whether the wrong model name is visible in the shipped hub on real metal -- verified only in code and by a Python reproduction of the exact ask_service/prompt_adapter logic, not by a live Ask turn against .43 (sandbox cannot reach the LAN LLM).

Whether mesh_node and paired_device receipts carry the same wrong-model divergence: MeshRelayIntel and the paired delegation path were not exercised, and MeshRelayIntel may or may not expose active_model.
Whether the meeting-intel receipt (as opposed to Ask/Recipe) prints a correct model name end to end -- intel_plan.py freezes honest metadata, but the meeting receipt rendering path was not traced.

result.pillar: DICTATION — speak, and text appears where you work
result.verdict: The desktop hold-to-talk path is the healthy one: press→admit→record→release→seal→Whisper→text_processor→voice-macro dispatch→DIR pipeline→preview-or-type is fully wired, with a cancellation fence on every publication path, and 732/750 dictation-selected Python tests pass. The browser path built in Phase 118/119 is where it frays: MicButton's click-to-toggle streams over a WebSocket that runs a full independent Whisper pass on every 600 ms chunk whose "partial" result no component in web/src consumes, holds the server audio floor on a 30 s lease it never renews, collapses every named server refusal into a generic "Dictation did not finish", and in the Speak room hands its already-pipelined text into /api/dictation/remote, which runs the whole DIR pipeline a second time on the same utterance (the route's own comment calls re-running it "a lie" and offers a raw:true flag the caller never sets). Separately, 16 dictation integration tests are RED on main because they grep web/src/pages/cores/DictationCore.tsx for markup that moved into pages/cores/dictation/*, so the pillar's UI regression fence is down and the repo's documented `uv run pytest` command fails. The DIR-01 plan's own evidence harnesses (measure_dictation_latency.py, both demo scripts) now crash inside build_pipeline because they carry no admission.
works: Desktop hold-to-talk is complete end to end: press admits one dictation.session, a refusal tears the capture down, release retires the generation, seals the deadline, and discards unadmitted audio (holdspeak/runtime/dictation_capture.py:474-584).

The hotkey tail is intact: Whisper child under an admission, text_processor, voice-macro dispatch inside the same cancellation election, DIR pipeline, then desktop type through the kernel warrant (holdspeak/runtime/dictation_capture.py:103-316).

Wake word is fully wired: openWakeWord listener with self-healing audio-floor respect, armed capture window, hard iteration cap, and a stop that reaches an in-flight capture and cancels it (holdspeak/runtime/wake_glue.py:100-325).

Preview-before-type is real on both hold and wake: server-minted one-shot token, broadcast, type/discard routes, and a React consumer (holdspeak/runtime/dictation_previews.py:23-106, web/src/components/AmbientLayer.tsx:18-44).

The cancellation fence holds on every publication path including the error paths: pipeline-disabled, runtime-unavailable, and the bottom except-clause all return through _publishable/_elected_publication (holdspeak/dictation_runner.py:190-205, 298-318, 441-454).

Speech control signals (SpeechSessionRefused / SpeechProviderFailure) are never degraded to raw text; the pipeline executor and both runner entry points re-raise them (holdspeak/plugins/dictation/pipeline.py:109-114, holdspeak/dictation_runner.py:441-448).
Browser open mic (Speak room) is coherent: VAD segmentation, floor claim with a real heartbeat, and honest handling of a server-closed interval (web/src/lib/openMic.ts:41-102).

The DIR pipeline executor itself is solid: ordered stages, per-stage error isolation with short-circuit to the input text, ring buffer for introspection, on_run hook that cannot break a run (holdspeak/plugins/dictation/pipeline.py:83-171).

The CLI dry-run is properly guarded: named credential refusal before construction, egress disclosed from the frozen plan, buffered body published under the session election (holdspeak/commands/dictation.py:129-230).

/api/dictation/remote is the most mature delivery surface: client-stable idempotency claim, named terminal refusals, aimed-agent refusal instead of free-typing, pre-delivery fence (holdspeak/web/routes/dictation/pipeline.py:417-880).

Test evidence: 101 focused pipeline/router/runner unit tests green, 166 admission/CLI/wake unit tests green, 24 dictation integration tests green, 62 web dictation vitest tests green (all run with an isolated HOME).

broken.title: 16 dictation integration tests are RED on main; the pillar's UI regression fence is down
broken.evidence: `HOME=$(mktemp -d) uv run pytest -q tests/integration -k dictat` → `16 failed, 144 passed, 1 skipped`. All failures read a file that is now a 137-line shell: tests/integration/test_web_dictation_cockpit.py:8 (`_page()` reads web/src/pages/cores/DictationCore.tsx), failing at test_web_dictation_cockpit.py:23. The asserted markup moved into the split files, e.g. 'Search the journal' now lives at web/src/pages/cores/dictation/Journal.tsx:214 while tests/integration/test_web_dictation_journal.py:141 still greps DictationCore.tsx. Same pattern in test_web_dictation_correction_ritual.py:64/70/83/92, test_web_dictation_corrections_api.py, test_web_dictation_learning_digest.py, test_web_dictation_settings_api.py, test_web_dictation_trust_signals.py, test_web_project_kb_api.py.
broken.impact: The documented test command (`uv run pytest -q`, CLAUDE.md) fails on a clean main. Every invariant those guards existed to protect — no tab wall, focus-safe React-owned lists, journal search + Clear-all confirmation, the correction ritual wiring, the project-KB and runtime sections, device-local project scope — is now unenforced, so the next Speak refactor can silently delete any of them.

broken.title: Speak-room dictation runs the DIR pipeline twice on the same utterance
broken.evidence: web/src/pages/cores/dictation/InstrumentStrip.tsx:75 wires `onText={onReleased}`; web/src/pages/cores/dictation/useSpeakDeck.ts:193-198 routes onReleased→deliver; useSpeakDeck.ts:152 POSTs /api/dictation/remote with no `raw` flag. The text it sends has ALREADY been pipelined: the WS final pass calls process_transcript at holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice.py:512-521, and the open-mic leg calls transcribeWav with the default `pipeline=true` (web/src/lib/speakToFill.ts:141, web/src/lib/openMic.ts:68). /api/dictation/remote then runs the full pipeline again via _run_dictation_dry_run_text (holdspeak/web/routes/dictation/pipeline.py:806-826). The route's own comment at holdspeak/web/routes/dictation/pipeline.py:706-711 states a previewed final_text 'has already been through the pipeline; running it again would make the receipt a lie (the rewrite is not idempotent)' and provides `raw: true` for exactly this case.
broken.impact: Every sentence spoken in the Speak room pays two full classify+rewrite round trips, and the second rewrite operates on the first rewrite's output — so the delivered text is a rewrite of a rewrite. Two journal rows are written per utterance (source 'browser' then 'dictation'), doubling the perceived latency and corrupting the journal's one-row-per-utterance story.

broken.title: The streaming mic claims the server audio floor for 30 s and never renews it
broken.evidence: holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice.py:428 calls _claim_browser_audio_floor, which acquires with `lease_seconds=30.0` (holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice_support.py:75). VoiceTypingSession._expire_locked frees any leased claim once the lease lapses (holdspeak/voice_typing.py:57-67). Nothing in the ws_dictation_stream handler (holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice.py:386-560) calls session.renew. Contrast the HTTP open-mic path, which heartbeats every FLOOR_RENEW_MS = 10 s (web/src/lib/openMic.ts:85-93, web/src/lib/audioFloor.ts:14-17).
broken.impact: Hold the click-to-toggle mic open for more than 30 seconds and the server silently believes nobody owns the microphone. The global hotkey, the wake listener, or a meeting can then claim the floor and start capturing while the browser stream is still recording and sending chunks — two capture owners on one microphone, which is precisely the condition the one-floor arbiter exists to prevent.

broken.title: Every 600 ms chunk gets a full Whisper pass whose result is thrown away
broken.evidence: web/src/lib/micStreamSession.ts:21 sets CHUNK_INTERVAL_MS = 600 and micStreamSession.ts:73-84 ships each chunk. holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice.py:468-478 transcribes each chunk independently and emits it as a `partial`; holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice.py:494-496 then re-transcribes the whole concatenated audio for the final. Client-side the only consumer is `onPartialRef.current?.(event.text)` at web/src/desk/components/MicButton.tsx:224, and grep across web/src shows `onPartial` appears ONLY inside MicButton.tsx (lines 48, 61, 76, 77, 224) — no caller ever passes it. Each transcribe takes the runtime's transcription_lock (holdspeak/runtime/dictation_capture.py:389).
broken.impact: A 30-second utterance triggers ~50 wasted Whisper invocations plus one real one, all serialized on the same lock the hotkey path needs. The user sees no progressive text at all, contradicting MicButton.tsx:3-4 ('streaming transcription fills the target field with progressive Whisper corrections') and the WS docstring's 'progressive Whisper result' (holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice.py:392). Isolated 600 ms fragments are also the worst case for Whisper hallucination, so the partials would be wrong even if something rendered them.

broken.title: Named WebSocket failures collapse to 'Dictation did not finish', and interval-closed is unhandled on the streaming mic
broken.evidence: The server sends structured refusals: holdspeak/web/routes/system/voice.py:474-480 and 527-545 include `reason`, `failure_category`, and `mic_interval: closed`. The client type has none of those fields (web/src/lib/micStreamSession.ts:11-14), MicButton reads only `event.error` (web/src/desk/components/MicButton.tsx:225-231), and dictationFailure maps a plain Error to 'unknown' (web/src/lib/dictationRecovery.ts:115-135 → DICTATION_FAILURES.unknown at :81-87). micIntervalClosed (web/src/lib/speakToFill.ts:129) is called only from web/src/lib/openMic.ts:70, never on the WS path. Worse, after an error the server returns without a `final`, so pendingFinal resolves to "" on close (micStreamSession.ts:56-65, 116) and MicButton.stopSession overwrites the real failure with 'no_speech' (MicButton.tsx:259-263).
broken.impact: A refused session, an exhausted child budget, a held audio floor, a revoked authority, and a genuinely silent recording are all presented to the user as either 'Dictation did not finish' or 'No words were detected'. The Sol Amendment 3 contract ('the interval closed, click again') is implemented server-side and ignored client-side for the mic that every desk text field uses.

broken.title: Retained-audio recovery is unreachable in production for every browser mic
broken.evidence: savePendingVoice has exactly one non-test caller: web/src/lib/speakToFill.ts:181, inside stopAndTranscribe. Grep across web/src shows stopAndTranscribe, startCapture and cancelCapture have NO non-test callers — MicButton uses startStreamSession exclusively (web/src/desk/components/MicButton.tsx:234) and FirstWords likewise (web/src/desk/components/FirstWords.tsx:107). So the `draftScope` prop never persists audio, and loadPendingVoice (MicButton.tsx:96) / retryPendingTranscription (MicButton.tsx:207) can never find any. The 'Captured audio is retained locally.' copy at MicButton.tsx:324 and the 'Retry retained audio' label at MicButton.tsx:295 are therefore dead UI.
broken.impact: When transcription fails, the captured audio is gone — the user must speak the whole thing again. The recovery affordance the failure copy promises never appears. The tests that cover it (web/src/desk/components/MicButton.test.tsx:108-140) pass only because they mock loadPendingVoice to return a buffer, so the suite reports a feature that production can never enter.

broken.title: build_pipeline without an admission raises, breaking the DIR-01 evidence harnesses
broken.evidence: holdspeak/plugins/dictation/assembly.py:297-302 raises SpeechSessionRefused(SESSION_NOT_ADMITTED) whenever there is no admission and no runtime_factory test seam. Proven: `build_pipeline(DictationConfig())` → `RAISED SpeechSessionRefused speech_session_not_admitted`. Callers with no admission: scripts/dictation_enrichment_demo.py:158, scripts/journal_e2e_demo.py:132, and scripts/measure_dictation_latency.py:294 (via run_dictation_pipeline, whose except-clause re-raises fatal speech signals at holdspeak/dictation_runner.py:619-626).
broken.impact: The latency-measurement harness the DIR-01 plan names as its reference evidence (docs/internal/PLAN_PHASE_DICTATION_INTENT_ROUTING.md §9, DIR-R-001/003) and both enrichment demos crash on the first line of work. Nobody can regenerate the phase's own performance evidence on this main.

broken.title: Live path skips the whole pipeline when the LLM runtime is unavailable, contradicting DIR-F-011 and the CLI
broken.evidence: holdspeak/dictation_runner.py:349-355 (and the duplicate at :541-547) return the raw text as soon as `result.runtime_status != "loaded"`, BEFORE pipeline.run is ever called. But assembly is built for graceful degradation: holdspeak/plugins/dictation/assembly.py:8-13 documents 'the pipeline still ships, but with llm_enabled=False so the intent-router stage is skipped', and assembly.py:113-126 still appends the non-LLM KbEnricher. The CLI does it the documented way: holdspeak/commands/dictation.py:176-179 prints 'running with intent-router skipped' and then runs the pipeline at :199.
broken.impact: With the runtime down, kb-enricher (which DIR-R-004 requires to be pure template substitution and never touch the LLM) silently never runs on the live typing path. `holdspeak dictation dry-run` shows the user enrichment output that their actual dictation will never produce — the introspection surface lies about the live path.

broken.title: Real audio duration and transcription timestamp are dropped between capture and pipeline
broken.evidence: holdspeak/runtime/dictation_capture.py:183 and holdspeak/runtime/wake_glue.py:382 compute `audio_duration_s=len(audio)/16000.0` and pass a real `transcribed_at`. holdspeak/runtime/dictation_processing.py:51-60 accepts both parameters and never forwards them to process_transcript. holdspeak/dictation_runner.py:264-274 hardcodes `audio_duration_s=0.0` and `transcribed_at=datetime.now()`. Proven at runtime: passing audio_duration_s=12.5 and transcribed_at=2020-01-01, the pipeline saw `0.0` and the current wall clock.
broken.impact: Utterance.audio_duration_s — a DIR-01 §6.4 contract field (holdspeak/plugins/dictation/contracts.py:27) — is 0.0 for every live utterance on every path. Any user-authored transducer stage that keys on utterance length (a plausible 'long dictation gets a different treatment' rule) is silently broken, and the journal/telemetry can never report how long anyone actually spoke.

broken.title: run_dictation_pipeline is dead production code duplicating the live entry point
broken.evidence: holdspeak/web_runtime.py:32 is the only occurrence of run_dictation_pipeline in that file — it is imported and never called (grep for run_dictation_pipeline across holdspeak/ returns only dictation_runner.py definitions plus that import). The single non-test caller is scripts/measure_dictation_latency.py:294, itself broken. The function body (holdspeak/dictation_runner.py:457-632, ~176 lines) is a near-verbatim duplicate of the live run_pipeline_corrections_only (holdspeak/dictation_runner.py:277-454) with skip_target_detection hardwired False. tests/unit/test_dictation_runner.py:47-246 drives the dead copy in 6 tests.
broken.impact: Two hand-maintained copies of the dictation pipeline orchestration exist; a fix applied to one silently misses the other. Six unit tests report coverage of 'the dictation pipeline' while exercising code no user can reach.

broken.title: max_total_latency_ms is documented as a hard pipeline ceiling but nothing enforces it
broken.evidence: docs/internal/PLAN_PHASE_DICTATION_INTENT_ROUTING.md:364 declares `max_total_latency_ms: int = 600  # hard ceiling; if exceeded, short-circuit next time`, mirrored at holdspeak/config/meeting.py:369. DictationPipeline.run (holdspeak/plugins/dictation/pipeline.py:83-171) never reads a budget, never tracks a prior overrun, and never short-circuits on time. Grep for max_total_latency_ms in holdspeak/ shows it used only for the ×5 cold-start cap (assembly.py:236) and the rewriter's extra-pass budget (assembly.py:122).
broken.impact: A slow model makes every dictation slow forever; the promised self-protection ('short-circuit next time') does not exist. Raising the setting in Settings changes cold-start tolerance and rewrite passes but not the thing its name and doc describe.

broken.title: The streaming mic suspends the AudioContext and zeroes the level meter every 600 ms
broken.evidence: web/src/lib/micStreamSession.ts:75-83 calls endHold() then beginHold() on every chunk tick. web/src/lib/micSession.ts:315-329 endHold() calls idle() whenever the open mic is off; idle() (web/src/lib/micSession.ts:175-188) disables the tracks, calls context.suspend(), emits level 0, and sets phase 'suspended'. beginHold only restores phase 'held' after awaiting ensureSession (micSession.ts:298-312).
broken.impact: During an active streaming dictation the mic phase lamp reads SUSPENDED roughly 1.6 times a second and the level meter drops to zero on each tick — the lamp that micSession.ts:9 calls 'the lamp that never lies' reports 'nothing is captured' while audio is being captured. The repeated AudioContext suspend/resume is also unnecessary churn on the capture graph.

broken.title: The documented no-pipeline speak-to-fill seam is unreachable; every field mic now runs the DIR pipeline
broken.evidence: holdspeak/runtime/dictation_capture.py:345-356 documents transcribe_audio as 'the NO-PIPELINE seam ... a speak-to-fill is the user typing with their voice, not a dictation run ...
